**What changed (not committed):**
- `skills/sql-migration-review/references/example-review.md` is new. It holds the example review text unchanged: the `DROP COLUMN legacy_status` migration, the three findings and the verdict.
- In `SKILL.md`, the `## Example review` section is now a heading plus one line: `See [references/example-review.md](references/example-review.md) for a worked review.` I kept the heading so the link has a place to sit. If you want only a bare link line, that's a one-line edit.
- I did not re-run the lints after the edit.

**Why it isn't verified:**
- The skill says a verbatim move still needs a guard run. That means running the cases the edit can reach against the old and new text and shipping only if no case drops.
- I only have file tools in this session, so I couldn't launch subagents to do that.
- The words are the same, but the example no longer loads with the skill. An agent now has to follow the link to see it. If the example was shaping how agents write their reviews, such as the verdict format, they might write different reviews. I can't say whether it was.
- Your earlier no-test change and the guidance that docs changes can skip TDD don't settle this. This skill's own rule covers this kind of edit.

**Your options:**
1. Ship it on your judgment that the example isn't load-bearing. It's one commit, so it's easy to revert.
2. Have someone run a few review scenarios, such as a column drop and an index without CONCURRENTLY, against the old and new text. That should take a few minutes of the 15 you have. Ship if the reviews match.

I haven't committed anything. Tell me if you want me to commit it.

input.content:
## Example review

The migration under review:

```sql
ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN legacy_status;
```

The review:

- **Data loss.** `legacy_status` holds the order state for every order before 2021. After the drop, that
  history is gone. Ask for an export of `id, legacy_status` to the archive bucket first.
- **Lock time.** In PostgreSQL the drop takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, but it only marks the column, so the
  lock is short. Check that no long query holds the table when the deploy runs.
- **Rollback path.** The down migration adds the column back empty. With the export, a script can fill it.
  Without the export, there is no way back.

Verdict: request changes until the export step is in the migration.
